title: Tenant preview cadence and rollback contract for private/on‑prem activations
creator: Priya Menon
description: Problem statement: Customers adopting Private/VPC/on‑prem instances frequently ask for a repeatable, predictable preview cadence and clear rollback guarantees. Current ad‑hoc previews cause blurred responsibility between PM, Eng, and Customer Success and inflate failure budgets. Goal: define a quarterly tenant preview cadence, a minimal rollback contract (technical + operational), and an activation checklist that can be used for all enterprise on‑prem engagements. Scope: preview cohorts, feature gating, compatibility checks, rollback triggers, runbook ownership, and OKR alignment. Out of scope: billing changes and custom contractual SLAs (handled by sales/legal).
milestones: Draft preview cohort taxonomy (internal short/medium/long previews) - 2026-01-20
Engineering acceptance criteria & API gating hooks merged - 2026-02-18
Finalize rollback contract and publish runbook - 2026-03-18
success_metrics: Mean time to rollback <= 30 minutes in pilot tests
0 critical incidents in customer pilot windows attributable to platform incompatibility
Activation runbook used without major edits by CX in 2/3 pilots
rollout_plan: 1) Define cohorts and eligibility criteria; 2) Implement lightweight API gating hooks and telemetry toggles in runtime-1.22 branch; 3) Run internal dry-run with dev tenants; 4) Execute 3 customer pilots staggered across weeks with strict go/no-go checkpoints; 5) Capture telemetry for OKR dashboards; 6) Publish public runbook and tenant activation checklist into Confluence and share with Sales/CX. Rollback contract: minimum viable guarantees (version pin, data retention guidance, rollback SLA window, clear escalation path to oncall).
risks: Incomplete kernel/quantization parity across customer onprem hardware leading to degraded inference quality
Network/VPC misconfiguration during pilot causing false-positive failures
Legal/contract friction if rollback guarantees perceived as commercial SLA
Engineering bandwidth conflicts with runtime-1.22 stability sprint
